Assumptions: 1. BEFORE = the same reactor under conventional operation: 15-day (360 h) HRT, 66.15 m3/d biogas, 63.63% CH4, 151.07 kWh/d (55,140 kWh/yr). All AFTER scenarios keep this reactor; only retrofits and operations change.

2. BIOGAS +40% - DOABLE AT EVERY STAGE: co-digestion FW+GW +44.96% (PubMed 35882315); PS/FW 1:3 +52% (PMC10241376); NaOH pre-treatment +40-55% (Springer 10.1007/s12649-023-02350-x); thermal 50 C +40% (PMC10979283); thermophilic operation raises kinetic rates 2-3x (PMC3811223). The 500 scenarios sweep +40.00% to +50.00%.

3. HRT TO HOURS - DOABLE ONLY WITH TWO ADDITIONS: (a) FEED SOLUBILIZATION by pre-treatment - hydrolysis is the rate-limiting step; NaOH cuts technical digestion time 79.6% (PMC8303515). (b) BIOMASS RETENTION inside the same tank - carriers/granules/membranes keep methanogens 20-80 days while liquid passes in hours (PMC9672170; PMC8703433). With both, 4-12 h HRT is proven (UASB/AnMBR/IC literature).

4. WHY A PLAIN MIXED TANK CANNOT DO HOURS (stage R6): fully mixed means biomass leaves with the effluent, so SRT = HRT. Methanogen doubling time 1-10 days; below ~3 days HRT they wash out. No operational trick changes this - it is a mass-balance limit, not an opinion.

5. THE RETROFIT LADDER: R1 thermophilic + co-digestion (3-5 days, no hardware) -> R2 + pre-treatment (2-4 days) -> R3 co-digestion synergy (4-7 days, simplest) -> R4 + carriers in same tank (0.5-2 days) -> R5 + full solubilization (4-12 HOURS). Climb the ladder as far as the feed and budget allow.

6. ELECTRICITY: rises 40-76% (more than biogas) because CH4 content climbs from 63.63% to 62-75% as pre-treatment and co-digestion enrich the gas. Electricity = methane x 3.5892 kWh/m3, gross before parasitic loads.

7. CAVEATS: hourly HRT needs soluble feed - pre-treatment is what converts solids to soluble COD. Pre-treatment and carriers add cost that must pass an ROI check. Research-based simulation, NOT plant measurement; pilot testing required before investor or grant claims.
